content: Magnesium oxide is an antacid that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of acid indigestion and upset stomach. Common side effects include diarrhea and allergic reactions. For adults, the FDA-approved indications for magnesium oxide include relief of acid indigestion and upset stomach. The recommended dosage for antacid use is one tablet taken twice daily or as directed by a physician. For magnesium supplementation, the dosage is one to two tablets daily or as directed by a physician. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium oxide in adults, whether guideline-supported or not. In pediatric patients, the safety and efficacy of magnesium oxide have not been established. Similarly, there is limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium oxide in pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or not. Contraindications for magnesium oxide are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include not exceeding two tablets in a 24-hour period or using the maximum dosage for more than two weeks without the advice and supervision of a physician. Magnesium oxide may have a laxative effect. Patients with kidney disease should consult a doctor before use. Additionally, individuals taking prescription drugs should consult a doctor or pharmacist, as antacids may interact with certain medications. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should seek advice from a healthcare professional before using magnesium oxide. The product should be kept out of reach of children. Adverse reactions reported include laxative effects. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experiences and postmarketing data for magnesium oxide. Drug interactions with magnesium oxide are not well-documented in the drug label. For specific populations, there is no FDA guidance on the use of magnesium oxide during pregnancy, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, pediatric use, geriatric use, or in specific gender, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised populations. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals are advised to consult a healthcare professional before use. The Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) has not provided guidance on the use of magnesium oxide in pregnant women. Magnesium oxide is administered orally. There is limited information regarding monitoring requirements for this medication. Information on IV compatibility is also limited. Overdose data, including chronic overdose, is not well-documented in the drug label. The pharmacology of magnesium oxide includes limited information on its mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. Clinical studies on magnesium oxide are also limited. Magnesium oxide tablets contain 240 mg of magnesium per tablet. The product should not be used if the imprinted safety seal under the cap is broken or missing. It should be stored at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). There is limited information available regarding patient counseling for magnesium oxide. The interaction between alcohol and magnesium oxide has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their doctor about the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The brand name for magnesium oxide is MagGel®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names.
